title: A Machine Learning Approach for Improving the Accuracy of Gridded Precipitation With Uncertainty Quantification
summary: Merges precipitation products and rain-gauge observations using machine learning to generate gridded rainfall estimates with spatially varying uncertainty for Vietnam.
significance: Shows how uncertainty can accompany the precipitation inputs that support hydrological prediction.
caveat: Use 2026 for the issue citation, optionally adding first online in 2025. The dataset covers Vietnam at 0.1-degree resolution over 2001–2010; avoid implying a U.S. operational precipitation product.

title: Designing an inundation monitoring and real-time urban flood forecasting system: a synthetic study
summary: Combines physical flood simulations, sparse inundation observations, and a vision transformer to reconstruct and forecast urban flood depths in a synthetic study.
significance: A direct example of linking rainfall scenarios, sensor placement, and rapid inundation forecasts in one framework.
caveat: Explicitly retain synthetic-study wording. Reported 20–50% improvement compares forecasts with and without inundation observations within the study; it is not a demonstrated operational performance claim.

title: Detroit Arsenal: Mapping Infrastructure Systems and Risk in a Critical Defense Region
public_byline: In partnership with the U.S. Office of Naval Research and collaborating universities
caveat: The displayed title and subtitle are combined here. No complete public conventional author list located; cite the institutional byline or confirm full credits. Creation date is repository metadata, not a claimed formal publication date.

title: Matching Urban Flood Sensor Placement to Monitoring Objectives Using Bayesian Optimal Experimental Design
caveat: No final journal record verified.

title: Reimagining How Flood Warnings Can Inform Decision-Making and Community Actions
summary: Proposes a flood early-warning framework that connects physical forecasting, human behavior, and decision science through uncertainty-aware support and feedback from communities and decision-makers.
significance: A particularly direct public source for explaining the integrated physical, human, and decision-science vision of the project.
caveat: This is a proposed framework and research perspective; do not describe it as a deployed system or demonstrated reduction in flood losses. Publisher gives first publication as 23 June 2026, while some institutional records use the issue date of 1 June.
figure_candidate: Figure 1 presents the physical, human/social, and decision-science framework and feedback loops. It is a particularly relevant candidate if exact reuse terms are verified.

title: Representing Uncertainty in Extreme Precipitation Using a WRF Ensemble
caveat: Author display names follow the public manuscript title page. Repository metadata expands Brian F. Jewett and omits Kevin’s middle initial. Public manuscript states submitted to JGR: Atmospheres; no final journal record verified.

title: Significant Rural Contributions to Severe Coastal Urban Flooding Through Flow Connectivity
summary: Examines how flow connections convey runoff from surrounding rural areas into severe coastal urban flooding.
caveat: The published title adds “Severe” to the report/preprint title. The preprint is the same work and is not counted separately.

title: Ten feet tall and invincible: How institutional culture shapes flood resilience at two U.S. Army installations
summary: Examines how institutional culture shapes flood resilience at two U.S. Army installations.
caveat: Published online September 24, 2026; the publisher record currently gives an online-first page range rather than volume and issue.

title: The Value of Forecasters‐in‐the‐Loop in Real‐Time Flood Forecasting in the Age of Machine Learning
summary: Compares machine learning and operational flood forecasts that incorporate human forecasters, highlighting the continuing value of forecaster judgment.
caveat: Comparisons use California–Nevada River Forecast Center operational forecasts and lead times up to 96 hours; do not generalize to all forecasting centers.

title: A Multifidelity Estimator of the Expected Information Gain for Bayesian Optimal Experimental Design
summary: Combines models of different fidelities to reduce the computational cost of estimating information gain for Bayesian experimental design.
significance: Provides a general computational foundation for deciding which measurements are most informative when high-fidelity simulations are expensive.
caveat: Demonstrations are a nonlinear benchmark and a turbulent-flow calibration problem. Do not imply the paper demonstrated flood-sensor deployment. Its unbiasedness is relative to the high-fidelity estimator mean.

title: AI Improves the Accuracy, Reliability, and Economic Value of Continental-Scale Flood Predictions
summary: Pairs Errorcastnet with the National Water Model to produce ensemble flood predictions with uncertainty estimates across the contiguous United States.
significance: Connects improvements in prediction and reliability to the potential decision value of flood forecasts over one- to ten-day lead times.
caveat: Economic value is assessed through the paper's cost-loss decision analysis. Avoid presenting percentage gains as realized monetary savings or universal accuracy improvements.

title: Bayesian Covariance Uncertainty for Adaptive Pilot-Sampling Termination in Multi-fidelity Uncertainty Quantification
caveat: No final journal publication verified.

title: CAMELSH: A Large-Sample Hourly Hydrometeorological Dataset and Attributes at Watershed-Scale for CONUS
summary: A public hourly hydrometeorological dataset covering 9,008 U.S. catchments, with observed hourly streamflow for 3,166 catchments and records spanning 1980–2024.
significance: Supports reproducible hydrological modeling and machine learning at the hourly scale relevant to rapid flood processes.
caveat: Do not state that all 9,008 catchments have streamflow observations or that the time series have no missing observations.

title: Optimal Stopping for Sequential Bayesian Experimental Design
caveat: No journal or accepted conference publication verified; use 2025 for the original preprint, optionally indicating the 2026 revision.

title: Pluvial flood impacts and policyholder responses throughout the United States
summary: Combines flood insurance claims, streamflow, and precipitation records to examine rainfall-driven flood damage and insurance uptake outside mapped 100-year floodplains.
significance: Highlights flood impacts beyond conventional high-risk zones and the challenge of sustaining risk awareness and insurance participation.
caveat: The 87.1% pluvial-claim result applies only to the analyzed subset of NFIP claims outside mapped 100-year floodplains, not all U.S. flood claims.

title: Reducing Uncertainty in Multijurisdictional Urban Stormwater Systems Under Climate Extremes

title: The Detroit Arsenal Flood: 2014 and beyond
public_byline: A collaboration Between UMich, BSU, and UIUC to study flood resilience, Funded by the ONR
caveat: The page credits Joseph Nigro as creator but does not give a complete conventional author list. Use its institutional byline or confirm the full author credits.

title: Connectivity in urbanscapes can cause unintended flood impacts from stormwater systems
summary: Examines the 2014 Southeast Michigan flood to show how connections among drainage networks, natural channels, and urban surfaces shape inundation.
significance: Provides a strong physical motivation for treating flood hazards across connected urban systems.
caveat: Findings derive from the studied urban system and modeled design configurations. Figure reuse permission was not verified.
figure_candidate: Figure 2: flood maps for the 11 August 2014 Warren, Michigan event. Figure 1: key urban flooding concepts.

title: Urban flooding is intensified by outdated design guidelines and a lack of a systems approach
summary: A policy brief on how outdated design assumptions and fragmented planning can intensify urban flooding.
caveat: A separate policy brief accompanying the urban-connectivity research article; do not label it another original research study.

title: VIME: Visual Interactive Model Explorer for Identifying Capabilities and Limitations of Machine Learning Models for Sequential Decision-Making
venue: Proceedings of the 37th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST ’24)
summary: An interactive visual toolbox helps users investigate sequential machine learning models through what-if scenarios and identify incorrect decisions.
significance: Contributes an approach to making model limitations visible to people evaluating AI-supported decisions.
caveat: Primary author and university sources verify the citation and mechanism; ACM direct retrieval failed. University description reports evaluation with 14 ML experts. Do not claim evaluation with operational flood forecasters. The software is licensed; do not label it open source.
